full_judgment:
That 0.54 acres of land of DP Plot No. 3539 of 4532 of DP Khatian No. 975 of Mouza Sannayasgachi, PS Keshobpur District-Jessore belonged to the petitioner's father late Reazuddin Sheikh. During field survey under Rules 28 and 29 of Tenancy Rules, 1955 the aforesaid land was wrongly recorded in the name of respondent No.4 and others against which the petitioner filed appeal under Rule 31 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955 which was registered as Appeal Case Nos. 34806, 34807 and 34808 and were heard and disposed of by judgment dated 21-12-1999 by the Settlement Officer, Jessore allowing the appeals of the petitioner and accordingly, the aforesaid DP Khatian No. 975 was made. Thereafter, on the approach of the respondent No.4, respondent No.1, in excess of the jurisdiction vested in him by law, passed an illegal order on 10-7-2001 directing the respondent No.2 to make correction of the judgment and order passed in the aforesaid appeals whereupon the respondent No.2, Zonal Settlement Officer, Jessore Zone sent the aforesaid appeal cases to respondent No.3, Assistant Settlement Officer, Kaliganj, Jessore for rehearing the decided appeals vide memo No. 17 of 2002 with intent to nullify the judgment made in the appeals under Rule 31 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955. 

 6. Mr ABM Nurul Islam, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, submits that the appeal cases being Nos. 34806, 34807 and 34808 of 1999 in respect of the case lands were disposed of on 21-12-1999 vide Annexure A in favour of the petitioner by the Settlement Officer under Rule 31 of the Tenancy Rules, 1955 and thereby creating a new khatian in the name of the petitioner and this shows that the order of the  appellate authority has already been acted upon vide Annexure B. Mr Islam further submits that under Rule 42A of the SA & T Rules, 1955 the Director of Land Records has no legal authority whatsoever to pass an order over a judgment of appellate Court about after 19 months. Under Rule 42A of the said Rules, a Revenue Officer can only direct for correction of the judgment of the appellate Court when an entry in the Record of Rights has been procured by fraud and there is no case that the petitioner procured the appellate judgment by fraud. Thus, the impugned order passed by the Director of Land Records marked Annexure-C, under Rule 42A of the Tenancy Rules, 1955 is totally illegal and without jurisdiction. Mr Islam lastly submits that the Director of Land Records and Surveys is the Executive Head of the entire Land Records and. Surveys Directorate but the Tenancy Act or the Rules has nowhere given him a power to change/amend/correct an appellate judgment and, as such, the impugned order marked Annexure C is not sustainable in law and such an illegal order vitiates everything. 

 11. The petitioner has challenged Annexure C dated 10-7-2001 whereby the Director Land Records and Surveys passed the order under rule 42A of the EBT Rules 1955, directing the Zonal Settlement Officer, Jessore for correction of the judgment and order dated 21-12-1999 passed in the aforesaid Appeal Cases by the Settlement Officer under Rule 31 of the EBT Rules vide Annexure A to the writ petition. Admittedly, the petitioner filed the appeals as above under Rule 31 before the Appellate Officer (Settlement Officer) who having heard both the parties and considered the facts, circumstances and materials placed before him allowed the appeals on 21-12-1999 by creating a khatian in his name and  accordingly, a Khatian marked as Annexure B to the writ petition has been created in his name. It shows that the order of the appellate authority has been acted upon vide Annexure B.
